notes: Ten independently authored AQA-style AS Physics Mechanics and Materials questions, especially graph signs, slopes, signed area, total distance, axes, moments and practical gradients. Original practice, not AQA past-paper wording. Reading worked solutions is not independent mastery.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A displacement–time curve is modelled by s = 2t² − 8t + 3, with s in metres and 0 ≤ t ≤ 5 s. (a) Find the instantaneous velocity at t=0, 2 and 5 s. (b) Find the acceleration and the time of the change of direction. (c) Find the displacement and total distance travelled over 5 s. [7 marks]
markPoints: Differentiate s to obtain v = 4t − 8 m s⁻¹.
At t=0, v=−8 m s⁻¹.
At t=2, v=0; at t=5, v=+12 m s⁻¹.
Acceleration is the velocity gradient, +4 m s⁻².
The velocity changes sign at t=2 s, so the body reverses direction there.
s(0)=3 m, s(2)=−5 m, s(5)=13 m, so net displacement is +10 m.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate s to obtain v = 4t − 8 m s⁻¹. At t=0, v=−8 m s⁻¹. At t=2, v=0; at t=5, v=+12 m s⁻¹. Acceleration is the velocity gradient, +4 m s⁻². The velocity changes sign at t=2 s, so the body reverses direction there. s(0)=3 m, s(2)=−5 m, s(5)=13 m, so net displacement is +10 m. Total distance is |−5−3| + |13−(−5)| = 8+18=26 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A velocity–time graph consists of straight segments through (0 s,+4 m s⁻¹), (2 s,−4 m s⁻¹), (5 s,−4 m s⁻¹), and (8 s,+2 m s⁻¹). (a) Find the acceleration in each segment. (b) Find the times when the object changes direction. (c) Find its signed displacement and total distance from t=0 to 8 s. [8 marks]
markPoints: For 0–2 s the acceleration is (−4−4)/2=−4 m s⁻².
For 2–5 s the acceleration is 0 m s⁻².
For 5–8 s the acceleration is (2−(−4))/3=+2 m s⁻².
The first zero-velocity crossing occurs at t=1 s.
The second zero-velocity crossing occurs at t=7 s.
Signed area from 0–2 s is zero; 2–5 s is −12 m.
From 5–8 s the signed trapezium area is −3 m; total displacement is −15 m.
Distance is 4+4+12+4+1=25 m, adding positive and negative areas by magnitude.
questions.modelAnswer: For 0–2 s the acceleration is (−4−4)/2=−4 m s⁻². For 2–5 s the acceleration is 0 m s⁻². For 5–8 s the acceleration is (2−(−4))/3=+2 m s⁻². The first zero-velocity crossing occurs at t=1 s. The second zero-velocity crossing occurs at t=7 s. Signed area from 0–2 s is zero; 2–5 s is −12 m. From 5–8 s the signed trapezium area is −3 m; total displacement is −15 m. Distance is 4+4+12+4+1=25 m, adding positive and negative areas by magnitude.

graphSpec.description: Straight-line velocity segments with sign changes at t=1 s and t=7 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A moving object starts with velocity +4 m s⁻¹. An acceleration–time record shows a=−3 m s⁻² for 0–2 s, +1 m s⁻² for 2–6 s, and −2 m s⁻² for 6–8 s. (a) Determine the three changes in velocity. (b) Determine velocities at 2, 6 and 8 s. (c) Give all times in 0–8 s when the object actually reverses direction. Explain why the area under an a–t graph does not directly give distance. [8 marks]
markPoints: First velocity change: Δv=−3×2=−6 m s⁻¹.
Second velocity change: Δv=+1×4=+4 m s⁻¹.
Third velocity change: Δv=−2×2=−4 m s⁻¹.
Velocity crosses zero at t=4/3 s, 4 s, and 7 s, reversing at each crossing.
Area under an acceleration–time graph is change in velocity, not distance; distance requires the magnitudes of velocity–time areas.
questions.modelAnswer: First velocity change: Δv=−3×2=−6 m s⁻¹. Second velocity change: Δv=+1×4=+4 m s⁻¹. Third velocity change: Δv=−2×2=−4 m s⁻¹. v(2)=4−6=−2 m s⁻¹. v(6)=−2+4=+2 m s⁻¹. v(8)=2−4=−2 m s⁻¹. Velocity crosses zero at t=4/3 s, 4 s, and 7 s, reversing at each crossing. Area under an acceleration–time graph is change in velocity, not distance; distance requires the magnitudes of velocity–time areas.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A 5.00 kg trolley is on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A 60.0 N force acts horizontally towards the upper end of the slope, not parallel to the plane. Take g=9.81 m s⁻². (a) Resolve the horizontal force parallel and perpendicular to the plane. (b) Determine the parallel weight component. (c) Calculate acceleration up the plane and the normal reaction. [7 marks]
markPoints: The horizontal applied force component up the slope is 60cos30°=52.0 N.
The horizontal applied force pushes into the plane by 60sin30°=30.0 N.
The weight component down the slope is mg sin30° = 24.5 N.
The perpendicular component of weight into the slope is mg cos30° = 42.5 N.
Resultant up the slope is 52.0−24.5=27.4 N.
From F=ma, acceleration is 27.4/5.00 = 5.49 m s⁻² up the slope.
Normal reaction is mg cos30° +60sin30°=72.5 N; a horizontal push increases R.
questions.modelAnswer: The horizontal applied force component up the slope is 60cos30°=52.0 N. The horizontal applied force pushes into the plane by 60sin30°=30.0 N. The weight component down the slope is mg sin30° = 24.5 N. The perpendicular component of weight into the slope is mg cos30° = 42.5 N. Resultant up the slope is 52.0−24.5=27.4 N. From F=ma, acceleration is 27.4/5.00 = 5.49 m s⁻² up the slope. Normal reaction is mg cos30° +60sin30°=72.5 N; a horizontal push increases R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A uniform horizontal beam of length 4.0 m and weight 80 N is hinged at its left end. A 120 N load acts downwards 3.0 m from the hinge. An upward cable force acts at the right end, and the beam remains in equilibrium. (a) Find the cable force. (b) Find the vertical hinge reaction. (c) A separate pair of equal and opposite 25 N parallel forces is separated by 0.30 m. State and calculate the moment of that couple. [6 marks]
markPoints: The uniform beam weight acts at its centre, 2.0 m from the hinge.
Clockwise moment about hinge =80×2.0+120×3.0=520 N m.
Cable tension T satisfies 4T=520, hence T=130 N upwards.
Vertical force balance: hinge reaction +130−80−120=0.
The vertical hinge reaction is +70 N upwards.
A couple has zero resultant force and moment 25×0.30=7.5 N m, independent of choice of pivot.
questions.modelAnswer: The uniform beam weight acts at its centre, 2.0 m from the hinge. Clockwise moment about hinge =80×2.0+120×3.0=520 N m. Cable tension T satisfies 4T=520, hence T=130 N upwards. Vertical force balance: hinge reaction +130−80−120=0. The vertical hinge reaction is +70 N upwards. A couple has zero resultant force and moment 25×0.30=7.5 N m, independent of choice of pivot.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: An object starts with v=−4.0 m s⁻¹. From t=0 to 4.0 s it has constant acceleration +2.0 m s⁻²; from t=4.0 to 8.0 s acceleration is −1.0 m s⁻². (a) Calculate v at 4 and 8 s. (b) Find the time of its change of direction. (c) Calculate signed displacement and total distance for 0–8 s. (d) Explain whether stopping at the final instant means a reversal. [8 marks]
markPoints: The initial velocity crosses zero at t=2.0 s, so reversal occurs there.
Signed displacement 0–4 s is zero: average velocity (−4+4)/2=0.
Signed displacement 4–8 s is (4+0)/2×4=+8 m.
Total signed displacement is +8 m.
Distance over 0–4 s is 4+4=8 m; over 4–8 s it is 8 m; total 16 m.
At t=8 s velocity is zero but no later motion is specified, so a further reversal cannot be inferred.
questions.modelAnswer: v(4)=−4+2×4=+4 m s⁻¹. v(8)=+4−1×4=0 m s⁻¹. The initial velocity crosses zero at t=2.0 s, so reversal occurs there. Signed displacement 0–4 s is zero: average velocity (−4+4)/2=0. Signed displacement 4–8 s is (4+0)/2×4=+8 m. Total signed displacement is +8 m. Distance over 0–4 s is 4+4=8 m; over 4–8 s it is 8 m; total 16 m. At t=8 s velocity is zero but no later motion is specified, so a further reversal cannot be inferred.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A displacement–time graph contains straight lines joining (t,s)=(0 s,+5 m), (2 s,−3 m), (5 s,−3 m) and (8 s,+9 m). (a) Find the velocity in each segment. (b) State the stationary interval. (c) Calculate when the object crosses s=0 on its first and last segments. (d) Calculate its displacement and total distance. [7 marks]
markPoints: The 0–2 s gradient is (−3−5)/2=−4 m s⁻¹.
The 2–5 s gradient is zero, so it is stationary for 2–5 s.
The 5–8 s gradient is (9−(−3))/3=+4 m s⁻¹.
First crossing: at −4 m s⁻¹ the object goes from +5 m to 0 in 1.25 s.
Second crossing: from −3 m at t=5 s, it takes 0.75 s, so t=5.75 s.
Displacement is final minus initial: +9−(+5)=+4 m.
Total distance is 8+0+12=20 m, without cancelling opposite directions.
questions.modelAnswer: The 0–2 s gradient is (−3−5)/2=−4 m s⁻¹. The 2–5 s gradient is zero, so it is stationary for 2–5 s. The 5–8 s gradient is (9−(−3))/3=+4 m s⁻¹. First crossing: at −4 m s⁻¹ the object goes from +5 m to 0 in 1.25 s. Second crossing: from −3 m at t=5 s, it takes 0.75 s, so t=5.75 s. Displacement is final minus initial: +9−(+5)=+4 m. Total distance is 8+0+12=20 m, without cancelling opposite directions.

graphSpec.description: Piecewise straight displacement curve: falls to −3 m, holds, then rises to +9 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A car's velocity–time graph is piecewise linear: (0 s,0 m s⁻¹) to (6 s,+12 m s⁻¹), then (+12 m s⁻¹) until t=10 s, then a straight line to (16 s,−6 m s⁻¹). (a) Calculate the initial and final acceleration. (b) Find the final reversal time. (c) Calculate total signed displacement and total distance in 16 s. [7 marks]
markPoints: Initial acceleration a=(12−0)/6=+2.0 m s⁻².
Final acceleration a=(−6−12)/6=−3.0 m s⁻².
The final velocity crosses zero 4 s after t=10 s, hence at t=14 s.
Displacement 0–6 s =½×6×12=36 m.
Displacement 6–10 s =4×12=48 m.
Displacement 10–16 s =[(12−6)/2]×6=+18 m, giving total +102 m.
questions.modelAnswer: Initial acceleration a=(12−0)/6=+2.0 m s⁻². Final acceleration a=(−6−12)/6=−3.0 m s⁻². The final velocity crosses zero 4 s after t=10 s, hence at t=14 s. Displacement 0–6 s =½×6×12=36 m. Displacement 6–10 s =4×12=48 m. Displacement 10–16 s =[(12−6)/2]×6=+18 m, giving total +102 m. Distance =36+48+½×4×12+½×2×6=114 m.

graphSpec.description: Car accelerates, travels at constant velocity, then brakes through zero and reverses.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: A force–time graph for a 0.600 kg trolley has two constant sections: +120 N from t=0 to 0.080 s and −40 N from 0.080 to 0.200 s. Initially the trolley has velocity −2.0 m s⁻¹. (a) Calculate the impulse of each section and the net impulse. (b) Determine the final velocity. (c) Explain why negative force does not necessarily imply negative displacement. [6 marks]
markPoints: Positive impulse =120×0.080=+9.6 N s.
Negative impulse =−40×0.120=−4.8 N s.
Net impulse is +4.8 N s (area with signs).
Initial momentum p=0.600×(−2.0)=−1.2 kg m s⁻¹.
Final momentum p=−1.2+4.8=+3.6 kg m s⁻¹; final velocity is +6.0 m s⁻¹.
Force determines acceleration and change of momentum, whereas displacement depends on velocity over time; opposite force can merely slow an object.
questions.modelAnswer: Positive impulse =120×0.080=+9.6 N s. Negative impulse =−40×0.120=−4.8 N s. Net impulse is +4.8 N s (area with signs). Initial momentum p=0.600×(−2.0)=−1.2 kg m s⁻¹. Final momentum p=−1.2+4.8=+3.6 kg m s⁻¹; final velocity is +6.0 m s⁻¹. Force determines acceleration and change of momentum, whereas displacement depends on velocity over time; opposite force can merely slow an object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.series: Original AQA-style Physics mechanics graph confidence
questions.prompt: In a free-fall investigation, a student plots vertical displacement s (m) against t² (s²). Two points on a straight best-fit line are (0.040 s², 0.196 m) and (0.160 s², 0.784 m). Release is approximately from rest with negligible drag. (a) Calculate the gradient and infer g. (b) Explain why plotting s against t² should be linear. (c) State two sensible ways to improve confidence in g. [6 marks]
markPoints: From s=½gt² the gradient is g/2.
Therefore g=2×4.90=9.80 m s⁻².
For release from rest and constant g, s is proportional to t², making a straight line through the origin ideally.
Collect more pairs over a wider t² range and use a best-fit line rather than two raw readings.
Repeat runs and/or use electronic timing to reduce random timing uncertainty; check any systematic intercept.
questions.modelAnswer: Gradient = (0.784−0.196)/(0.160−0.040)=0.588/0.120=4.90 m s⁻². From s=½gt² the gradient is g/2. Therefore g=2×4.90=9.80 m s⁻². For release from rest and constant g, s is proportional to t², making a straight line through the origin ideally. Collect more pairs over a wider t² range and use a best-fit line rather than two raw readings. Repeat runs and/or use electronic timing to reduce random timing uncertainty; check any systematic intercept.
